questions.subject: Internal Security
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's Defence Cyber Agency (DCA):
1. It replaces CERT-In for all cyber security in India
2. It handles both offensive and defensive cyber operations for armed forces
3. It was established in 2019
4. It is a tri-service agency under the Chief of Defence Staff
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — DCA does NOT replace CERT-In. DCA handles MILITARY cyber operations (protecting military networks, offensive cyber warfare capability). CERT-In (under MeitY) handles CIVILIAN cyber security (national incident response, coordination). They have different mandates — DCA is defence-specific, CERT-In is national civilian infrastructure. Both operate independently. DCA HQ: New Delhi, draws personnel from all 3 services.

questions.subject: Internal Security
questions.question:
With reference to India's Coastal Surveillance Network:
1. Chain of 46 coastal radar stations provides continuous monitoring
2. National Automatic Identification System (NAIS) tracks vessel movements
3. India has zero vulnerability from the sea after these measures
4. Fishing vessel registration and ID has been mandated for all boats
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — vulnerabilities persist: small fishing boats can still go undetected, gaps between radar coverage areas exist, Pakistan's use of fishing boats for smuggling/terror (26/11 route), deep sea surveillance limited. Coastal radar chain (Phase I: 46 stations, Phase II: expansion): provides surface picture up to 25 NM. NAIS: transponder-based tracking of large vessels. Challenge: 2 lakh+ fishing boats — many don't carry transponders. Multi-layered approach needed: technology + community policing (fishermen as eyes/ears).

questions.subject: Internal Security
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's space-based surveillance:
1. India's defence satellites are entirely built by private companies
2. EMISAT is an electronic intelligence satellite
3. These satellites support military reconnaissance along borders
4. India uses RISAT (Radar Imaging Satellite) for all-weather surveillance
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India's defence satellites are primarily built by ISRO (not private companies). RISAT series (SAR radar: works day/night, through clouds — critical for border surveillance). EMISAT (2019, DRDO payload): signals intelligence — intercepts enemy radar/communication emissions. Cartosat (high resolution optical): mapping/surveillance. Private sector is entering (data analytics, small sats) but ISRO/DRDO lead construction. Defence Space Agency coordinates military space requirements.

questions.subject: Internal Security
questions.question:
With reference to the Armed Forces Special Powers Act (AFSPA):
1. It allows armed forces to search, arrest, and use force (including shoot to kill) in disturbed areas
2. Section 4 provides immunity to armed forces from prosecution without Central government sanction
3. Jeevan Reddy Committee (2005) recommended repeal of AFSPA
4. SC in Extra-Judicial Execution Victims vs UOI (2016) held AFSPA doesn't give license to kill
questions.explanation: All correct. AFSPA (1958 for NE, 1990 for J&K): grants special powers in 'disturbed areas' declared by Centre/Governor. Powers: shoot to kill on suspicion (Section 4(a)), arrest without warrant, search without warrant, destroy arms dumps. Section 6: no prosecution without Central sanction. Jeevan Reddy Committee (2005): recommended repeal, replace with Unlawful Activities Act provisions. SC (2016, Justice Madan Lokur): every death must be investigated, army can't claim immunity for fake encounters, FIR must be registered.

questions.subject: Internal Security
questions.question:
Consider the following about terror financing channels:
1. Hawala, cryptocurrency, and trade-based money laundering are used
2. India's Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND) monitors suspicious transactions
3. Cash Transaction Reports (CTR) above ₹10 lakh must be filed with FIU
4. FATF evaluates countries including India on anti-money laundering compliance
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Terror financing methods: hawala (informal value transfer), crypto (pseudonymous), trade-based laundering (over/under invoicing), charitable organizations (front organizations), extortion (NE insurgents). FIU-IND (under Finance Ministry): receives CTRs (cash >₹10 lakh) and Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from banks/FIs. FATF Mutual Evaluation (India 2024): India found largely compliant, placed in 'Regular Follow-up' category (positive). Enforcement: ED (PMLA), NIA (terror financing), IT Dept (Benami transactions).

questions.subject: Internal Security
questions.question:
With reference to India's Multi-Agency Centre (MAC):
1. It is an intelligence-sharing mechanism hosted by IB
2. It operates 24/7 sharing real-time threat intelligence
3. It was revamped after the 26/11 attacks
4. State-level equivalents are called SMACs (Subsidiary MACs)
questions.explanation: All correct. MAC (under IB, post-Kargil 1999, revamped post-26/11 2008): real-time intelligence sharing platform connecting: IB, RAW, military intelligence, NIA, NSG, CRPF, state police special branches, NTRO, financial intelligence. Operates 24/7 from IB HQ. SMACs in every state capital: mirror MAC at state level for local intelligence coordination. Pre-26/11 failure: agencies had fragments of intelligence but didn't share — terrorists exploited this gap. MAC ensures: no intelligence silo, immediate dissemination of threat inputs across agencies.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about the National Rural Livelihood Mission (DAY-NRLM):
1. It organizes rural poor women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs)
2. India has 90+ lakh SHGs with 10+ crore women members
3. SHG-Bank Linkage provides micro-credit without collateral
4. It is the world's largest community institution-based poverty alleviation programme
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. DAY-NRLM (restructured from SGSY in 2011): universal social mobilization of rural poor into SHGs. Scale: 90+ lakh SHGs, 10+ crore women members, ₹7+ lakh crore cumulative bank credit. SHG-Bank Linkage (NABARD pioneered, 1992): groups save collectively, get bank loans at SHG level (no individual collateral needed). Lakhpati Didi target builds on this base. World's largest: no other country has community-institution-based poverty programme at this scale. Focus: financial inclusion + livelihood diversification + social empowerment.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
With reference to PM-SVANidhi (Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi):
1. It provides micro-credit (₹10,000-₹50,000) to street vendors
2. No collateral or guarantor required
3. Interest subsidy of 7% provided on timely/early repayment
4. Digital payments adoption among vendors is incentivized through cashback
questions.explanation: All correct. PM-SVANidhi (June 2020, initially for COVID recovery): Working capital loan: first tranche ₹10,000, second ₹20,000, third ₹50,000 (progressive). No collateral/guarantor. 7% interest subsidy on regular repayment. Monthly ₹100 cashback for digital transactions (UPI/QR adoption). Target: 50 lakh+ vendors. Extended beyond COVID. Letter of Recommendation from ULB/TVC serves as identity. Transformed: previously unbanked vendors now in formal credit system. Also provides: skill development, insurance cover link.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) and PM Gati Shakti:
1. Both have been fully completed with all projects delivered on time
2. PM Gati Shakti is the PLANNING platform; NIP is the PROJECT pipeline
3. Gati Shakti ensures all ministries' infrastructure plans are geospatially coordinated
4. NIP identified 7,400+ projects worth ₹111 lakh crore (2020-25)
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — NIP/Gati Shakti have NOT been fully completed. Many projects face delays (land acquisition, environmental clearances, funding gaps). NIP: framework for identifying and tracking infrastructure investments. Gati Shakti: digital platform ensuring NEW projects are planned holistically (avoids: road built but no electricity, port built but no rail connection). Together: NIP identifies WHAT to build, Gati Shakti ensures HOW to plan it cohesively. Actual completion depends on execution by individual ministries/states.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's data economy:
1. India generates the world's 3rd largest volume of data
2. Data centres in India are growing rapidly (expected 1 GW capacity by 2025)
3. India allows completely unrestricted cross-border data transfers without any conditions
4. Data localization debates centre on: sovereignty vs free flow of data
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India does NOT allow completely unrestricted cross-border data transfers. DPDP Act 2023: allows transfer to countries NOTIFIED by government (positive list approach — government will notify which countries have adequate data protection). Transfer to non-notified countries restricted. RBI mandates: payment data must be stored in India (localization). Earlier draft PDP Bill was stricter (mirror copy requirement) — DPDP is more balanced but NOT 'unrestricted'. Tension: MNCs want free flow; government wants sovereignty over citizen data.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
With reference to India's urban flooding problem:
1. Encroachment on natural drains and wetlands worsens urban flooding
2. Impervious surfaces (concrete) prevent rainwater absorption into ground
3. Indian cities have outdated drainage designed for much lower rainfall intensity
4. Climate change is increasing the frequency of extreme rainfall events over Indian cities
questions.explanation: All correct. Urban flooding (Mumbai 2005/2017/2024, Chennai 2015, Hyderabad 2020, Bengaluru 2022): multi-causal. Drains encroached (slums, construction on nullahs). Concrete/asphalt: 80%+ runoff vs 20% in natural areas. Drainage: designed for 25mm/hour rainfall — cities now get 100-200mm in hours. Climate change: IPCC confirms more intense precipitation events over South Asian cities. Solutions: sponge city concept (permeable surfaces), wetland restoration, stormwater harvesting, real-time flood forecasting (IFLOWS-Mumbai), strict building regulations enforcement.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's healthcare tourism:
1. India attracts approximately 5-7 lakh medical tourists annually
2. Treatment costs in India are 60-90% lower than Western countries
3. India is among top 5 medical tourism destinations globally
4. Medical visa category was introduced specifically for health tourists
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Medical tourism: India receives 5-7 lakh+ medical tourists (pre-COVID peak, recovering). Cost advantage: cardiac surgery ($5,000 vs $100,000 in US), hip replacement ($7,000 vs $40,000). Top hospitals: Apollo, Medanta, Fortis, AIIMS (for specific procedures). India: among top 5 (alongside Thailand, Singapore, Turkey, Mexico). Medical visa (M visa): introduced for foreigners seeking medical treatment in India — separate from tourist visa, allows longer stays and multiple entries. Heal in India initiative promotes this. Foreign exchange earnings: $5-7 billion/year from health tourism.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
With reference to India's food processing sector:
1. India is the world's 2nd largest food producer but wastes ~$14 billion of food annually
2. India's food processing sector is 100% developed with zero post-harvest losses
3. Mega Food Parks provide common infrastructure for food processing units
4. PM Kisan Sampada Yojana promotes food processing infrastructure
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India loses approximately 5-16% of production in post-harvest wastage (fruits/vegetables up to 30-40%). Cold chain coverage is only 4% of perishable produce. PM Kisan Sampada (₹6,000 crore): integrated cold chain, mega food parks, food processing units, backward-forward linkages. Mega Food Parks (42 approved): cluster approach with common infrastructure (cold storage, testing labs, packaging). PLI for food processing (₹10,900 crore): Ready-to-Eat, marine products, fruits/vegetables. Target: double food processing from 10% to 25% of agri output.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's substance abuse problem:
1. National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use (2019) was India's first comprehensive study
2. All narcotic substances including alcohol are regulated under a single legislation
3. De-addiction centres operate under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
4. Approximately 3.1 crore Indians use cannabis and 2.3 crore use opioids
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — alcohol is NOT regulated under NDPS Act. Alcohol regulation is a STATE subject (State List, Entry 8). Each state has its own excise policy. NDPS Act covers: narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances (cannabis, opium, heroin, synthetic drugs, meth). Bihar has alcohol prohibition; Goa has cheap alcohol policy — states decide. National Survey 2019 (AIIMS-MoSJE): first pan-India study revealing scale. Punjab 'chitta' crisis, NE opium belt, Mumbai party drugs — regional patterns differ.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to 'Missing Women' phenomenon in India:
1. The concept was highlighted by Amartya Sen (1990)
2. It refers to the deficit of women due to sex-selective abortion, neglect, and violence
3. India's overall sex ratio improved from 933 (2001) to 943 (2011)
4. The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act regulates sex determination
questions.explanation: All correct. Amartya Sen (1990 essay): estimated 100 million 'missing women' globally due to gender discrimination. India's sex ratio: improving but still adverse (943/1000, Census 2011; SRS 2021 shows 1,020 females/1000 males at birth → Sex Ratio at Birth improving). PCPNDT Act (1994, amended 2003): prohibits sex determination/disclosure, regulates ultrasound clinics. Despite law: sex-selective abortion continues in pockets (Haryana, Punjab, parts of UP/Gujarat). Beti Bachao Beti Padhao targeting districts with worst Child Sex Ratio.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's waste management crisis:
1. India generates 62 million tonnes of solid waste annually
2. All Indian cities have achieved 100% source segregation of waste
3. Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 mandate source segregation
4. Only 20-25% of waste is processed/treated; rest goes to landfills
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — most Indian cities have NOT achieved 100% source segregation. Only a few (Indore, Surat, Mysuru — Swachh Survekshan toppers) have near-complete segregation. Most cities: mixed waste collection persists. SWM Rules 2016: mandate wet/dry/hazardous segregation at source, bulk generator responsibility, construction debris management, bio-methanation. Challenges: public awareness, informal waste picker integration, waste-to-energy (controversial — emissions concerns), landfill remediation (legacy dumpsites like Ghazipur catching fire).
